cues.speaker: tariq
cues.text: Claude, GTA 6 comes out soon, and every influencer on my feed claims you can make twenty grand clipping live streams with AI. Is that actually real?

cues.speaker: claude
cues.text: Let us break it into three honest parts: what people claim, how to do it free, and the copyright reality.

cues.speaker: tariq
cues.text: Start with the hype. What are they telling people to do?

cues.speaker: claude
cues.text: Take an eight-hour streamer broadcast, have an AI detect the funny moments, convert it to nine-by-sixteen, and spam it across TikTok and Reels.

cues.speaker: tariq
cues.text: So literally just re-uploading other people's gameplay without editing?

cues.speaker: claude
cues.text: That is the entire business model.

cues.speaker: tariq
cues.text: Okay, but how much does the AI software cost?

cues.speaker: claude
cues.text: Zero dollars. An open-source tool called OpenShorts just dropped on GitHub with eight thousand stars.

cues.speaker: claude
cues.text: MIT licensed. You paste any stream link, and local AI extracts viral clips, crops the facecam, and generates animated captions automatically.

cues.speaker: tariq
cues.text: Wait, it handles face tracking and captions too? What am I supposed to do?

cues.speaker: claude
cues.text: Press publish and pray YouTube's algorithm does not notice.

cues.speaker: tariq
cues.text: And that brings us to part three: is the money real?

cues.speaker: claude
cues.text: The views are real. But the footage belongs to Rockstar, and YouTube actively demonetizes reused content with zero commentary.

cues.speaker: tariq
cues.text: Plus fifty thousand kids will be clipping the exact same stream on launch day.

cues.speaker: claude
cues.text: Exactly. In a gold rush, the people getting rich are not the clippers, it is the developers building the clipping tools.

cues.speaker: tariq
cues.text: So I should not quit my engineering job to farm GTA clips?

cues.speaker: claude
cues.text: You are a senior developer, Tariq. Go review your pull requests.
